g1.label: 1. Tom's not at his desk. He's ___ to lunch.
g1.why: ‘Gone’ is used because Tom is still away — he hasn't come back yet.

g2.label: 2. I've ___ to Berlin three times.
g2.why: ‘Been’ is used for a completed visit — the person has returned.

g3.label: 3. We've ___ to that restaurant before.
g3.why: ‘Been’ is used for a past experience — the person is back now.

g4.label: 4. She's ___ to the shops. She'll be back soon.
g4.why: ‘Gone’ is used because Maria is still at the shops — she hasn't returned yet.

g1.label: 1. My brother ___ his keys again!
g1.why: ‘My brother’ is singular, so the present perfect uses ‘has lost’.

g2.label: 2. These trees ___ a lot since we planted them.
g2.why: ‘These trees’ is plural, so the present perfect uses ‘have grown’.

g3.label: 3. The company ___ its results yet.
g3.why: ‘The company’ is singular, so the present perfect negative uses ‘hasn't announced’.

g4.label: 4. Somebody ___ the window.
g4.why: ‘Somebody’ is singular, so the present perfect uses ‘has broken’.

g5.label: 5. Petrol prices ___ again this month.
g5.why: ‘Petrol prices’ is plural, so the present perfect uses ‘have gone up’.

g6.label: 6. She ___ to drive.
g6.why: ‘She’ is singular, so the present perfect uses ‘has just learned’.

g1.label: 1. I've ___ finished my homework — five minutes ago!
g1.why: ‘Just’ shows an action finished a very short time ago.

g2.label: 2. I have ___ sent the email.
g2.why: ‘Already’ shows something happened sooner than expected.

g3.label: 3. Has the bus arrived ___?
g3.why: ‘Yet’ is used in present perfect questions asking if something has happened.

g4.label: 4. We haven't decided where to go ___.
g4.why: ‘Yet’ is used at the end of negative present perfect sentences.

g5.label: 5. They have ___ left for the airport.
g5.why: ‘Already’ shows the action happened before now, sooner than expected.

g1.label: 1. I have ___ ridden a horse before.
g1.why: ‘Never’ (= not at any time) fits the meaning ‘this is my first time’.

g2.label: 2. My grandfather has ___ used a smartphone.
g2.why: ‘Never’ expresses that he has not had this experience at any time.

g3.label: 3. Have you ___ visited London?
g3.why: ‘Ever’ is used in present perfect questions asking about experience.

g4.label: 4. This is the strangest thing that ___ to me!
g4.why: ‘Thing’ is singular, so the present perfect uses ‘has happened’.
